name: Northumbria University, Newcastle

settingEvidence.evidence: Our city-centre campus means most of our accommodation is within walking distance, helping you cut down on everyday transport costs.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK students on full-time courses starting in 2027 (2027/28), subject to UK Government approval. A classroom-based foundation year (Business/Social Sciences/Humanities) is £5,760, a placement year £2,010 and a study abroad year £1,510 (2027/28).

source.evidence: If you are studying on a Full-Time course the fee for your first year of study for 27/28 will be £10,050* the maximum chargeable fee.

livingCosts.text: University residences cost about £121–£239 a week in 2026/27, depending on the room: the cheapest is a Stephenson bedroom at £121.05 and the dearest a Camden Court studio at £238.92. Standard en-suite rooms are about £165–£195 a week. Contracts are mostly 43 or 44 weeks.

contextual.summary: Home-fee applicants who meet any one of Northumbria's contextual criteria and firmly accept their offer need fewer UCAS tariff points on results day (for example 96 instead of 112).
contextual.typicalReduction: 120-point course to 104 points; 112-point course to 96 points; 72-point course to 56 points

criteria.detail: Your home address on your UCAS application is in POLAR4 quintile 1 or 2 (an area with a low rate of progression to higher education).
Your home address on your UCAS application is in IMD decile 1-4 (areas of higher deprivation; deciles 1-4 are the bottom two quintiles).
You have spent time in care. You must complete the care questions in your UCAS form; Northumbria may ask for evidence.
Black, Asian or Minority Ethnic origin (an under-represented group at Northumbria). UCAS passes this on late, so you complete Northumbria's Contextual Offer Enquiry short form.
You are eligible for free school meals.
Adult learner: over 21 at the start of your programme.
You listed unpaid caring responsibilities (not including parenting) on your UCAS form; Northumbria may ask for evidence.
Estranged from parents: not in contact with or supported by parents.
Physical and/or mental health condition, long term illness or learning difference.
Student parent: you are a parent or have parental responsibilities for a child under 17.
You have served or are serving in the UK Armed Forces, or a parent or guardian has served or is serving.
First generation: you do not have a parent who holds a higher education qualification.
Refugee or humanitarian status, or currently claiming asylum (extra evidence is required).
Member of the Gypsy, Traveller, Roma, Showman or Boater communities.
You took part in the HAF+ programme or the Holiday Hope (London) programme.

contextual.rulesText: You are eligible if you meet any one of the criteria and firmly accept your offer via UCAS. You must be eligible for home fees, apply through UCAS (with the information entered on your application) and hold Level 3 qualifications that attract UCAS tariff points. Your UCAS offer isn't changed: the lower points are applied when results arrive. The reduction can't be combined with a reduced offer from Northumbria's other Supported Entry Scheme or Extenuating Circumstances. If you miss the lower points on results day, Northumbria guarantees a place on an extended degree (foundation year) course if you firmly accepted.

source.evidence: You are eligible for contextual admissions if you meet any of the criteria below and firmly accept your offer via UCAS.

programmes.name: Destination Northumbria
programmes.summary: A support programme with peer support, social and on-campus events, webinars and podcasts to help you prepare for starting at Northumbria.
programmes.whoCanApply: Applicants with home fee status who meet at least one eligibility criterion, such as living in a low-progression area, free school meals, care experience, being first in the family to go to university, caring responsibilities or being estranged from parents.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Home fee status plus at least one of: POLAR4 quintile 1-2 or IMD decile 1-4 area; care experience; Black, Asian or Minority Ethnic origin; free school meals; adult learner (over 21 at the start); unpaid caring responsibilities; estranged from parents; physical or mental health condition, long term illness or learning difference; student parent; served in the Armed Forces; parent or carer in the Armed Forces; first generation (no parent with a higher education qualification); refugee or humanitarian status or claiming asylum; Gypsy, Roma, Traveller, Showman or Boater communities; LGBTQ+ or trans, non-binary and other diverse identities.

notes: No 2028-entry offers yet (checked 2026-10-21): every course page shows 'Entry Requirements 2027/28' and a September 2027 start, so all courses use 2027 entry.
Northumbria gives offers in UCAS tariff points, not grades: the standard offer is 112 points on all six courses recorded and the contextual offer is 96 points.
Northumbria is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry, and no course page names an admissions test.

Extended Degrees (4 years including a foundation year) exist for these subjects. The Economics Extended Degree (UCAS Z018) has a standard offer of 72 UCAS points and a contextual offer of 56 (https://www.northumbria.ac.uk/study-at-northumbria/courses/bsc-hons-economics-extended-degree-uusxic1/). The 2027/28 fee for a classroom-based foundation year is £5,760.

Aspirational offers: Northumbria typically makes standard tariff offers to applicants whose predicted grades are equivalent to up to three or four grades below its standard entry criteria, depending on the programme, and in most cases adds a reserve 'dual offer' for the Extended Degree (https://www.northumbria.ac.uk/study-at-northumbria/admissions/northumbria-university-entry-requirements-essential-information/aspirational-offers/).
Halls prices come from each residence page, which says 'Prices for 2026/27': the lowest is the Stephenson Bronze bedroom (£121.05 a week) and the highest the Camden Court studio (£238.92 a week).
Evolve (post-16 workshops for Year 12-13) is booked by schools and colleges rather than applied for by individual students, so it is not listed as a programme.
